one_month_reasoning: The window from 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-04 contains Vicor's Q3-26 report. The date is not yet announced; Vicor reported on Oct 21 2025, Apr 21 and Jul 21 2026, so ~Oct 20-21 is likely. Revenue is pre-announced at >30% q/q (>$186M, release of 2026-09-30). The move will come from the first disclosure of how much of the >= ~$29M Sep-16 licence royalty is back-royalty versus run-rate, the Q4 guide and product GM. Late-October hyperscaler capex calls also fall in the window. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways. Reversal risk follows a +63% run from the August close ($187.68) and fresh Form 144 sales on Oct 1-2. Licence-news days have added 10-20% (Sep 11, 16, 22). I centre at ~$300, about 2% below spot, with a 28% one-month log-sd: 95%/3.5 = 27%, widened slightly for the earnings disclosure. This is unchanged from round 1 except for a slightly wider spread, in line with the supervisor's view that the report is binary-ish.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (1) SOTP P/E on NTM recurring EPS at the horizon, interest income excluded: product $3.66 x 26.5x (11-peer CY2027 median) + royalty $2.22 x 22x + $10.3 net cash = $156.2, and (2) a 2028-31 FCF DCF (WACC 10.5%, g 4%) valued at the horizon = $159.5. 0.5 x 156.2 + 0.5 x 159.5 = $157.8 -> $158. The fixed $60M licence (ends Q3-27), the Q3-26 back-royalty, the 2025 $45M settlement and the 2026 tax benefits are excluded.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: SOTP. Product NTM EPS ex-interest $3.66 x 26.5x = $97.1. Recurring royalty NTM EPS $2.22 x 22x = $48.8 (legacy $15.4M/qtr + new VPD ~$20-25M/qtr, less IP costs). Net cash ~$500M / 48.5M = $10.3. Total $156.2 (implied blended ~24.8x NTM recurring EPS of $5.89).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 product revenue $112.9M (10-Q). July guide of ~10% q/q to ~$158M with royalty at ~$20.4M ($15.4M legacy + $5M fixed licence) implies Q3 product ~$137M. 2027 $700M (+~45% on ~$480M 2026E) backed by one-year backlog $379.7M (+26% q/q) and book-to-bill >1. 2028 $900M (+29%) as Fab-2 starts (~1-year lead time from the Sep-2026 site purchase) and customer AI capex growth slows to +22% in the capex file's base case.

Q2-26 product GM = ($112.9M - $60.2M cost of product) / $112.9M = 46.7% (10-Q), depressed by one-time factory reorganisation that management expects to fade as utilisation rises (Q2 call). Partial recovery assumed.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 total opex $48.2M/qtr (SG&A $27.6M + R&D $20.6M) = ~$193M/yr; I allocate ~$15-20M/yr of it to IP enforcement (charged against royalties) and grow the rest ~10-15%/yr for headcount and Fab-2 start-up.

Forecast, not reported. Q2-26 legacy $15.4M is derived = Q2-26 royalty $30.426M (10-Q) less $15.0M recognised from the fixed $60M licence (Q2 call); 4 x $15.4M = $61.6M, taken as ~$60M/yr. Assumed renewed roughly flat when the two-year agreements expire (Q2 call: renegotiation 'based on business growth'); risk noted.

Signed 2026-09-16, two weeks before quarter-end, so a large part is likely back-royalty; the 10-Q policy recognises usage-based royalties as licensee sales occur. I take ~55-60% as run-rate (~$16-17M/qtr) rising to ~$25M/qtr in 2028 as the licensee ramps. This replaces my round-1 $35-40M/qtr by 2028.

inputs_detail.derivation: Product: CY27 ($357M GP - $200M) x 0.79 / 48.0M = $2.58; CY28 ($477M - $230M) x 0.79 / 48.5M = $4.02. Royalty: CY27 ($140M - $15M) x 0.79 / 48.0M = $2.06; CY28 ($160M - $20M) x 0.79 / 48.5M = $2.28. Interest income excluded (was +$15M/yr in product). Below consensus CY2027 $6.12-6.35 because consensus includes the fixed licence, Q3 back-royalty and tax benefits.

Median CY2027 forward P/E of 11 power-conversion / AI-power-chain peers = 26.55x (range 19.1x-41.1x). No premium: VICR product EPS grows faster from 2027 to 2028 (+51%), but the multiple is applied at the horizon to NTM (mostly CY2028) earnings, when growth into 2029 (~25-30%) is near the peer median next-year growth (29.5%); product GM (~47-53%) is below MPWR's; revenue is concentrated (10-K: the majority of Advanced Products revenue comes from one customer or a limited number of customers; no single-customer % is disclosed).

Inside the peer range, below the 26.5x median. Royalty income needs no fab capex (higher cash conversion than product earnings), which argues up. The licences run two years and are renegotiated (Q2 call), the new licensee's terms are undisclosed and the Q3 amount is partly back-royalty, and leverage rests on the ITC 337-TA-1484 determination (USITC target date 2027-09-20), which argue down. Raised from 15x, which the supervisor called punitive and which falls below the reconstituted peer range.

Cash $453.6M at 2026-06-30 and no financial debt (10-Q balance sheet: liabilities are payables, accruals and leases), plus the $14.3M CHIPS refund received 2026-07-13 (Q2 call), plus ~$300M operating cash flow over 15 months, less ~$220M capex for the Merrimack/Hooksett sites and Fab-2 fit-out (prices undisclosed) and ~$50M of the $150M buyback. Cut from ~$650M per the supervisor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF 2028-31 $223M / $330M / $448M / $564M on revenue $1.06B / $1.32B / $1.60B / $1.88B at 21-30% FCF margins. WACC 10.5%, terminal growth 4% (TV $9.0B). EV at the horizon $7.23B + net cash $0.50B = $7.73B / 48.5M sh = $159.5.

Lowered from 25-32% in round 1 for heavier Fab-2/3 capex (two NH sites, ~1M sq ft footprint) and a lower royalty share. H1-26 capex was $23.6M (10-Q) before the fab build.

bear.story: The base-rate path: VICR's 2018 (-51%), 2021-22 (-68%) and 2023-24 (-65%, monthly closes Jul-2023 $92.27 to Apr-2024 $32.38) retracements, and -53% from the Jun-2026 high to the Jul-2026 low inside this cycle. The Q3 royalty proves mostly back-payment (run-rate < $10M/qtr), the late-2027 renewals reprice down or 337-TA-1484 disappoints, product GM stays in the 40s and AI capex digests (Kalshi 21% for a 2027 recession). The market pays ~25x a ~$5.2 recurring NTM EPS, plus ~$10 cash. The probability is cut from 0.35 because the Q3 VPD contribution (>= ~$29M) is now verified and the net-cash floor is real.

base.story: Recurring NTM EPS ex-interest of ~$5.89 is delivered (product ~$700M in 2027, VPD ~$20M/qtr run-rate, legacy royalties renewed roughly flat). The market keeps part of VICR's long-standing premium: ~35x NTM recurring EPS + cash (~$216), or ~41x trailing GAAP EPS of ~$5.3 at the horizon (which still includes the fixed licence). That is below today's ~48x CY2027 consensus and ~62x recurring, and above my peer-based fair value ($158). The gap to fair value is deliberate: VICR has not ended any year since 2018 below 38x trailing EPS (year-end trailing P/E 48x, 137x, 225x, 101x, 94x, 38x, 345x and 42x for 2018-2025, from XBRL EPS and Twelve Data closes), so in my lane's base rate the premium compresses but does not vanish within 12 months. Lowered from $275 because the royalty run-rate evidence is lower than I assumed and to narrow the FV gap the supervisor flagged.

bull.story: VPD licensing becomes an industry toll: more OEM and hyperscaler licensees, an ITC exclusion order around Sep-2027 forces stragglers, renewals reprice up, the 2nd-gen VPD ramps in late 2027, and NTM EPS heads to ~$9. The market pays ~50x, as it does for MPWR at the top of the peer range today, plus cash. Trimmed from $500 because recurring royalty is now built at ~$20-25M/qtr rather than $35-40M.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 19.1x (ON) to 41.1x (MPWR). All are finviz next-fiscal-year P/E at the 2026-10-05 close. Every peer reports on a calendar year except ADI (October FY, ~2 months off), so the basis is CY2027. Forward EV/EBITDA is not shown: no source publishes it for these peers (citation fix 2026-10-06). StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' (mixed fiscal basis) is not used. MCHP (FY ends March, ~3 quarters off, and trough-cycle EPS) was considered and left out.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: VICR trades at 48.1x CY2027 consensus EPS ($6.35, finviz), an 81% premium to the 26.6x median, and at ~62x my CY2027 recurring EPS of $4.89. In fair value I use 26.5x (the median) on product earnings and 22x (lower half of the range) on recurring royalty earnings: a blended ~24.8x NTM recurring EPS, inside the peer range. My base scenario (~35x NTM recurring) sits above the median. That is a market-behaviour assumption from VICR's own valuation history, not a fair-value premium, and it is why my ladder median ($222) is above fair value ($158).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium in fair value. On growth: VICR's product EPS grows faster into 2028, but at the horizon the NTM multiple is applied to mostly-2028 earnings, and growth into 2029 (~25-30%) is near the peer next-year median (29.5%). On margins: product GM is 46.7% in Q2-26, below MPWR. On risk: customers are concentrated (10-K) and royalties rest on two-year licences renegotiated in late 2027 plus an ITC determination. Base rates argue against a durable fundamental re-rating: three prior AI/data-center re-ratings each gave back 51-68% within ~12 months. The royalty discount to the median (22x vs 26.5x) reflects short licence duration and the undisclosed back-royalty share, partly offset by zero capex intensity. Sell-side targets were not used. Changes from round 1: NVDA, AVGO (customers), ALAB, CRDO, MRVL (connectivity) and MTSI were dropped and AEIS, BELFB, NVT, APH, ON and TXN added, per the supervisor's comps review. The median moved from 27.6x to 26.6x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$145 VICR would trade at ~23x NTM recurring EPS ex-interest of ~$5.89 excluding ~$10/share cash, close to the bottom of the peer range (19.1x), and ~20% under the ~$184 pre-licence level of mid-September 2026. At that price the market would be saying the licensing leg failed: the Sep-16 licence royalty proved mostly back-payment, renewals repriced down, or 337-TA-1484 went against Vicor. It would also mean AI product orders were cut, with backlog back below ~$300M. Ordinary 95% volatility around my $222 median would not by itself take the stock there. Unchanged from round 1. The supervisor's $150 is close; I keep $145, below the Aug-2026 closing range ($187.68-$253.50, Twelve Data daily) that the stock fell through without a fundamental break. (Corrected 2026-10-06: the Aug-2026 range was $187.68-$253.50, not $150-$180; the stock last closed below $150 on 2026-03-30 at $142.22, before the VPD licence.)

reasoning: Round 2. I verified the supervisor's main findings against primary documents. 10-Q: Q2-26 product revenue $112.9M, royalty $30.4M, cash $453.6M, no financial debt, and the SynQor $28.56M payment on 2026-03-18 was an outflow. Q2 call: the $60M licence is recognised 15/5 then 10x4 and ends Q3-27, and a $14.3M CHIPS refund came in July. 8-K of 2026-08-27: a new $150M buyback. Releases of Sep 11, 16 and 30: Fab-2/3 sites bought, a non-exclusive VPD licence, Q3 >30%. From the 10-Q Q2 revenue, the July ~10% guide and the >30% guide, the new licence adds >= ~$28.7M in Q3. Because it was signed two weeks before quarter-end, I treat ~55-60% as run-rate. That cuts my 2028 royalty from $220M to $160M. Corrections taken: net cash ~$500M not ~$650M; the $28.6M moved out of the one-off list; royalty multiple 22x not 15x; peers rebuilt as an 11-name power set on one CY2027 basis (median 26.6x). Recurring NTM EPS at the horizon is $6.13 incl. interest ($5.89 ex-interest after the 2026-10-06 fix). Fair value: P/E SOTP $163 ($156.2 after the fix), DCF $160, blend $161 ($158 after the fix), below round 1's $176 mainly because of the lower royalty run-rate and cash. Reconciling FV with the ladder (the supervisor's main point for me): my FV is what peer multiples justify, and the ladder is where the market is likely to price VICR in a year. My lane's base rates cut both ways. VICR retraced 51-68% after each prior re-rating, and 5x winners show no positive drift afterwards. But VICR's year-end trailing P/E has been >= 38x every year since 2018, so the market premium historically compresses rather than disappears. I therefore cut the base scenario from $275 to $225 (~35x NTM recurring + cash), which narrows the base-to-FV gap from 56% to 40% and defends what remains with that history. Bear $140 (30%), base $225 (47%), bull $470 (23%) in a lognormal mixture (log-sd 0.35 / 0.28 / 0.33) give a median ~$222, mean ~$269, P(>= spot) 0.28 and P(>= $535) 0.08. That is below the supervisor's $248 median: I give more weight to the retracement base rate and the lower royalty run-rate. The scenarios reconcile to the ladder: the mixture median sits near the base price, and the probability-weighted scenario mean ($256) sits between FV and spot. Sell-side targets and option-implied data were not used. Citation fix 2026-10-06: other income ($15M/yr) was in product EPS while $10.3/share net cash was also added, a double count; EPS is now ex-interest. Legacy royalty relabelled 'estimate'; forward EV/EBITDA removed (unsourced); 337-TA-1484 target re-cited to the USITC IDS record; 95% realised vol re-checked on Twelve Data (95.2%). Fair value $161 -> $158, base $216, 12-month ladder shifted by 158/161.
